Interface Codec<A>

All Known Implementing Classes:
SealedCodec
public interface Codec<A>
How to write an A as JSON and read it back: a type class, resolved as a given.

Codecs see only JsonWriter and JsonReader, so they run on any backend. Malformed or unacceptable input is a JsonException with the value's path; a value that can't be written (a null field, NaN) is an IllegalArgumentException. encode is never passed null; a codec that has a JSON form for "nothing" (optional(Codec), nullable(Codec)) says so through isOptional().

Built in: String, the primitives and their boxes, BigDecimal, BigInteger, UUID, Instant, List, Set, Map<String, A>, Optional and forj's Either.

Records get a codec from record User(...) derives Codec, which forj's plugin turns into a call to deriveProduct(Function, Codec.Encoder, Codec.Field...), or by hand from product(Function, Codec.Field...).

    • field

      static <T,F> Codec.Field<T,F> field(String name, Function<T,F> getter, Codec<F> codec)
      A field whose codec is the given for its type. Pass the type arguments (Codec.<User, Long>field("id", User::id)): forj doesn't infer them from a method reference.

    • product

      @SafeVarargs static <T> Codec<T> product(Function<Object[],T> constructor, Codec.Field<T,?>... fields)
      A codec for a record (or any product) as a JSON object: constructor receives the decoded fields in the order given, boxed. Unknown fields are skipped; a missing field is an error unless its codec is optional; a repeated field is an error. 
      given Codec<User> codec = Codec.product(
        a -> new User((long) a[0], (String) a[1]),
        Codec.<User, Long>field("id", User::id),
        Codec.<User, String>field("name", User::name));

    • deriveProduct

      @SafeVarargs static <T> Codec<T> deriveProduct(Function<Object[],T> constructor, Codec.Encoder<T> encoder, Codec.Field<T,?>... fields)
      product(Function, Codec.Field...), with an encoder forj generates as straight-line code: deriveField(out, 0, user.id()); deriveField(out, 1, user.name()); .... Each call picks the deriveField for its component's type, so a long is written without boxing or a getter. Decoding is product's.

    • sealed

      static <T> SealedCodec.Builder<T> sealed(String discriminator)
      A codec for a sealed family of cases, each a JSON object naming its case in the discriminator field, which comes first: 
      given Codec<Payment> codec = Codec.<Payment>sealed("type")
        .when("card", Card.codec, p -> p instanceof Card c ? c : null)
        .when("cash", Cash.codec, p -> p instanceof Cash c ? c : null)
        .build();                 // {"type":"card","number":"4111…"}, {"type":"cash"}
      Each case keeps its own codec (usually a product(Function, Codec.Field...)). An unknown tag, a missing discriminator or one that isn't the first field is a decoding error; a value no case selects can't be encoded. Nothing checks that every case is listed (derives doesn't cover sealed interfaces yet), so a forgotten case fails when such a value is encoded.

    • nullable

      static <A> Codec<A> nullable(Codec<A> codec)
      null as a value, for types that use it to mean "absent". Not a given: plain Java null is opted into per field, with Codec.field(name, getter)(using Codec.nullable(codec)). A missing field reads as null, and a null field is written as null.
